_about: Published results of the Expert Survey on Progress in AI (ESPAI), run by AI Impacts among authors at top machine-learning venues. Numbers are copied from the survey write-ups cited per entry; nothing here is computed. Question wording changed between rounds (noted per entry), so the series is indicative, not a like-for-like time series. Add a new round as a new object; the site picks it up on the next build.

rounds.wording: Long-run effect of high-level machine intelligence: 'extremely bad (e.g. human extinction)'.
rounds.citation: Grace, Salvatier, Dafoe, Zhang & Evans (2018), 'When Will AI Exceed Human Performance? Evidence from AI Experts', Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research 62.

rounds.wording: Same question as 2016. AI Impacts' later re-aggregation put the 50% HLMI year for this round at 2060.
rounds.citation: AI Impacts (2022), '2022 Expert Survey on Progress in AI'.

rounds.wording: Same long-run question (median 5%, mean 9%), plus new questions on extinction or permanent severe disempowerment (median 5%, mean 16.2%) and on human inability to control AI (median 10%, mean 19.4%).
rounds.citation: Grace, Stewart, Sandkühler, Thomas, Weinstein-Raun & Brauner (2024), 'Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI'.
